intelligence.human_view: He reached back to a presentation he already loves — "those beautiful nice Smart Links like we used before" — and said: that is how contacts should look. Not a directory, not a settings screen: the Smart Link on the Smart Tab, one click to organize, edit, star, love. And the default is the machine doing the work: contacts auto-organized into lists, so nobody organizes by hand. The human clicks; the machine sorts. The same object does double duty: the Smart Mail topic pills are Smart Links on Smart Tabs too, which is why this law rides their fix — one object, one presentation, everywhere.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine your friends all have beautiful name cards on a bar — you tap one and it tidies itself, or you give it a star and it goes on your favorites list! And the cards sort themselves into groups all by themselves, so you never have to tidy them. That's how contacts should work.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, your contacts will look like those lovely Smart Links on the Smart Bar — tap one and it organizes itself, or you can change it, or give it a star so it goes on your favorites. And the system sorts them into lists for you, so you never have to do the organizing yourself.
intelligence.naya_view: CONTACTS ARE SMART LINKS ON SMART TABS. A CLICK ORGANIZES THE CONTACT; A CLICK CHANGES OR EDITS IT; A STAR OR A LOVE PUTS IT ON THE FAVORITES LIST. A NEW LIST IS MADE WITH AN EDIT BUTTON / A + BUTTON. BY DEFAULT THE SYSTEM ORGANIZES CONTACTS FOR THEM — AUTO-ORGANIZED INTO LISTS — SO NOBODY HAS TO ORGANIZE THEM BY HAND.
